text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code changes to a shared repository. Each time they do this, an automated build starts. The system compiles the code and runs tests to check that everything works correctly. This helps catch issues early, before they become big problems. CI pipelines make this process smooth and repeatable. They can build, test, and even prepare software for release. By using CI, teams find bugs faster, save time, and improve the quality of their software. It has become an essential part of working in agile and DevOps environments.
